page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-48 is a general-purpose server instance powered by the arm64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated physical cores utilizing the Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There are no bundled GPUs or local NVMe storage drives included with this instance type, and it does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The processor features 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware-level support for AES cryptography but lacking x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX or AMX.

Benchmark data indicates that the t2a-standard-48 delivers strong multi-core CPU performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 87022.37. However, single-core performance is relatively modest, with Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core benchmarks falling into the weak and average tiers respectively. Memory bandwidth is consistent, showing average performance across both small cached blocks (3391.09 GB/sec) and large uncached blocks (181.23 GB/sec read, 78.56 GB/sec write). Text processing and single-threaded decompression tasks represent notable performance bottlenecks, scoring in the weak category. For machine learning workloads, the instance achieves average prompt processing speeds on small and medium models, but text generation speeds drop to poor or weak tiers, especially as model size scales up to 70B parameters.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t2a-standard-48 leverages the high resource density of the Ampere ARM architecture to offer a balanced ratio of compute resources to memory without the overhead of hyperthreading. This makes it a viable option for scale-out workloads that benefit from physical core isolation and predictable multi-threaded execution. The instance is recommended for workloads such as static web serving, multi-threaded software compilation, database operations, and general-purpose application hosting.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-48 is an arm64 general-purpose server instance equipped with 48 dedicated physical cores on an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. It features 192.0 GB of RAM, translating to 4.0 GB of memory per core, with no bundled local storage or GPUs. The instance exhibits strong multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng benchmarks, though single-core processing and text-based operations are relatively weak. Memory bandwidth remains average, with read speeds of 181.23 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Lacking AVX and AMX extensions, it is not optimized for heavy vector math, which is reflected in its weak performance during large-scale LLM text generation. The t2a-standard-48 is recommended for multi-threaded workloads, static web serving, software compilation, and database operations where physical core isolation and balanced memory-to-CPU ratios are required.
